entry.title: Rogue Legacy 2 v1.2.0
entry.content:
Note: Please replace both the .apworld and the game mod files when updating to this version
### New Features - Added a new manor type using the YAML setting `manor_type` called "shop" which allows items to be purchased from the manor more like a re-stocking shop (very similar to Unfair Flips). There are 4 slots to buy from, and buying any item replaces it with a new item until that slot is exhausted. Items get more expensive the further into the shop you go. - The idea is essentially to allow a larger number of purchases from the manor than the vanilla branching manor layout provides. With the shop layout you can have many more (or less) items available for purchase in the manor. - Fabled weapons are now available in an AP run. They can be set to always be use-able, or can be unlocked as a progressive item for each class. - Burdens are select-able for AP runs as well now. The first time you connect to an AP world, the burden selection screen will appear. This will set the burdens for the entire run. The only way to change them after this point is to enable the Debug Keys in the Archipelago Settings and press "6" to re-open that screen (which will take effect the next time an heir is selected). - Earning XP can now give you AP items. The in-game mastery rank can be set to earn items either per-class or as an overall mastery level. Mastery level is only increased when an heir dies (or retires) and at that point you will get earn the locations for these checks.
### Improvements - Allow controller input in the connection dialog box - Changed YAML option `manor_depths_per_boss` to `manor_depth_percent_per_boss` to be more easily understandable, especially with the new manor type. - Added an in-game tracker for biome specific checks (blueprint chests, rune chests, journals, and memories) - It will show you the number of checks you've collected, the number of in-logic checks, and the total number of checks available for each type. If all checks for a given type in a biome are out-of-logic, the whole row will be dimmed. - This can be toggled on or off in the Archipelago Settings screen - Raised the limit on the maximum number of locations you can have for chests in the YAML options - Checks which were already released from outside the game (via admin console or a player completing their game) will now be skipped for pooled checks (chests and individual-type journal/memories). This essentially means you don't waste locations on chests that would grant an item which is already given.
### New Config Options
1. `manor_layout` - (tree/shop, default: tree), Tree layout is the existing layout. It uses the same branching tree as the vanilla manor does. The new options is "shop" which gives the repeated slot purchase layout described above. a. `manor_shop_depth` - (1-100, default: 25), How many purchases each slot holds in the shop manor layout. b. `manor_depth_percent_per_boss` (0-100, default 25), what percentage of manor purchases are added to logic for each boss kill. This replaces the existing `manor_depth_per_boss` with a more easily usable setting. 2. `fabled_weapons` - (randomized/soul_shop/unlocked, default: randomized), Randomized turns the fabled weapons into AP items which can be received. They are progressive on the class unlock, so the first one received unlocks the class and the second instance will unlock the fabled weapon. When set to soul_shop, the fabled weapons are still purchase-able in the soul shop (and always available), although they use their normal price and are realistically probably difficult to afford. This is mostly the same as just turning them off. When set to unlocked, they will always be available so long as their class is unlocked. 3. `mastery_checks` - (disabled/total/per_class, default: total), Allows XP earnings to unlock Archipelago items. Each level of mastery rank counts as a single check. These can be totaled over all classes or give specific checks for each class's own mastery levels. a. `total_mastery_levels` - (1-750, default 50), How many checks are associated with mastery levels when in total mode b. `mastery_levels_per_class` - (1-50, default 10), How many checks for each class are associated with mastery levels when in per_class mode. This will result in 15 * mastery_levels_per_class number of locations being added c. `mastery_progression_percent` - (0-100, default 50), What percentage of the mastery level locations may actually have useful items behind them. This essentially allows you to tweak what percentage of the mastery levels you may be required to achieve, even though you can still have more checks afterwards that may give non-essential benefits. d. `mastery_xp_multiplier` - (10-10000, default 300), How much the XP you earn is multiplied before being converted into mastery ranks. 100 means you get the same amount of XP as the vanilla game awards, but that can be very slow. Turning this higher allows you to get more mastery ranks in less time. This becomes essentially required if you dial up the number of mastery-rank locations since later levels require a lot of XP.
### Bugfixes
- More resilient save-handling. The sync between the AP server's state and the game's state should be stronger now. In addition, save recovery should be better. Archipelago runs now save backups similar the vanilla game runs and can restore them using vanilla's backup recovery screen. - Fixed a bug where stat upgrades weren't applied in specific scenarios mid-run (they instead waited until the next heir or certain triggers to apply).

entry.title: Gravity Circuit (MuratDev's Implementation) v1.0.0

entry.title: Slay the Spire II v1.4.2
entry.content:
> [!WARNING] > Both Slay the Spire II and this Archipelago Mod are in active development. As such, while this _is_ playable, expect there to be bugs and limited features. We appreciate your playtesting!
> [!IMPORTANT] > **Play on the game's beta branch.** Main-branch support is on thin ice but supported none the less: the mod still runs there, but it's largely untested and new game features might not be supported on it.
## Setup
For installation, YAML configuration, generation and connection instructions, see [the Slay the Spire II setup guide](https://github.com/dlueben1/Slay-the-Spire-2-Archipelago/blob/setup-docs-do-not-delete/world/spire2/docs/setup_en.md).
Archipelago **Launcher v0.6.7+** is required for generation. Install **STS2-RitsuLib 0.6.11+** separately.
The newest YAML Builder is at [sts2ap.terairk.dev](https://sts2ap.terairk.dev/#/builder), and the mod's **Mod Website & YAML Builder** button opens it. [sts2ap.net](https://sts2ap.net/#/builder) gets the new options later.
# Version Information
- **Archipelago Mod:** 2.2.3 - **APWorld:** 1.4.2 - **Slay the Spire II main branch:** v0.111.1 - **Slay the Spire II beta branch:** v0.113.1
# Changelist
A small release on top of 2.2.2.
1) New sight challenge: **Hidden Relics**. Your relics are unknown (locked icon, "?" counters) until a Relic Sight arrives, but they still flash, so you can work them out. A second Relic Sight makes relic rewards offer 2 to choose from. Doesn't work on ancients cus its annoying and i said so. 2) Eight new Boons: Ink Bottle, Medical Kit, Blue Candle, Preserved Insect, Torii and Turnip from the first game, plus Amphorae and Cursed Kettle which are my own fancy relics that i made up cus why not. - Could debate on these being 'Bonus items' but for now they're in the boons section. 3) Some Boon nerfs: Wayfinder is 3 free moves per run and shares them with Winged Boots, Second Wind works once per run and heals 35%, and Spring Cleaning gives one of its rewards at random. 4) Sight bonuses buffs: a second Map Sight also gives a free move once per act, and a second Pile Sight also draws 1 more card next turn the first time your draw pile is shuffled each turn. Rationale: buff the less cool ones 5) YAML Builder: a new Items & Hints section (starting items, starting hints, local and non-local items), and importing a YAML keeps the settings the builder doesn't ask about. 6) The mod's local files now live in one folder per AP slot under `mod_data/Archipelago`. Old files move there by themselves, and Local Save Management can forget old seeds. Hopefully this doesn't break stuff but the files/logs/saves were in like 4 different folders all nested weirdly so this will be easier to give advice to people in the future. 7) Fixes: Inky and Exposing only go on cards that target enemies (Inky used to crash on the others), Exposing shows its Vulnerable line on the card.
### Version compatibility
Use the updated APWorld and mod together. An older APWorld ignores Hidden Relics and the new Boons.
Everyone in a multiplayer lobby should use the same mod version and game branch.
Tested in singleplayer on the beta branch.
## Known Issues/Limitations
- **Main branch:** largely untested and gets no new features. Main-branch multiplayer might not be supported in a future release. - In multiplayer, AP menu rewards can only be claimed outside combat; Death Fragments are disabled. **Anytime** Ancient rewards are recommended.

entry.title: Crash Team Racing v0.3.0a6
entry.content:
## Discord
Come hang out on [Appie's Games Discord](https://discord.com/invite/HxXy4mKQ5E). Test builds, bug reports and YAML sharing all happen there.
Alpha6 is out! Thanks for all the alpha5 reports. This one fixes the Oxide Station softlock, a pile of custom track problems (unreachable crates, missing music, Relic-only tracks that wouldn't start) and quick savestates that mixed up races. It also adds Kart Setup in the pause menu during a race, race and cup rewards in the tracker, CNK letters on Inferno Island and author credits on custom tracks. The hub pause menu is reordered, pads and the tracker count shared checks, and Citadel City travel and cup win text are fixed. It's still an alpha, so 0.2.4 stays the stable release.
[Full notes on AP-Pie](https://beta.ap-pie.com/ctr/releases) · [Setup guide](https://ap-pie.com/guides/ctr)
## Before you try it - Use the alpha6 client and APWorld together. Your alpha5 YAML usually still works. Rooms made with alpha5 usually connect, but that is best effort: if one is refused, keep using the alpha5 client for it. Rooms made with alpha6 need the alpha6 client. Rooms from 0.2.x still need 0.2.4. - Quick saves (F5) made with alpha5 won't load. Make a new one.
## Fixed - Oxide Station pickups don't depend on a one-time race anymore. In new rooms each pickup either has a repeatable route or is left out, so a missed crate can't block you. Thanks Dex! - Custom track crates that can't be reached (Matsuri's first item box, one crate in Lockbox Adventure track 4) are out of the pool in new rooms, and crate logic is corrected on Sewer Speedway, Cortex Vortex, Country Speedway, Toasty Terrace, Royal Raceway and Green Hill Raceway. - Relic-only custom tracks start from their pad now. Before, a track with relics and a lap but no AI lines refused to start. - Seed downloads fetch a custom track's current music, Custom Tracks downloads music an installed track is missing, and a failed song start is tried again. A track that has no music of its own plays a random retail song instead of always Roo's Tubes. - Quick savestates stay with the race they were made in. Loading one from a different track, mode or room is refused instead of mixing things up. - When you walk up to a pad, the hint now covers weapon crates, Wumpa crates and Wumpa, also on cup tracks and boss garages. The "crates checked" count popups are gone. entry.title: Civilization IV v0.0.1r2
entry.content:
This is the release that 0.4 should have been, with lots of Resourcesanity fixes, as well as Wondersanity fixes.
### Changelog: New in 0.4.1: - Fur, Ivory, and Whale resources don't go obsolete anymore, regardless of the Resourcesanity settings. - Non-water resources now require The Wheel to be in logic (as it's impractical to connect them to the capital otherwise) - Receiving a city from another player (either through trade or capture) with a World Wonder sends the respective location check just as if you've built it. - Fixed Shrines attempting to send a location check - Prevented barbarians from spawning "AP" units
New in 0.4.0: - Resourcesanity is available in an initial form. A check is sent when you have at least one instance of a resource available in your capital, either by connecting it naturally or getting it via trade. The logic makes sure you have the techs needed to reveal and connect the given resource (or make a corporation for it in the case of Aluminum and Oil), and additionally requires Iron Working to connect Calendar resources (as the majority of them are placed in jungle on "normal" maps). You also aren't guaranteed to have every resource on every map and may need to generate another game to get all checks. - If Peekable Locations is set to either "Great People" or "All" in the YAML, the option to "bulb" a location will show the name of the item you're sending. In this initial implementation GPs are the only location that's peekable, it doesn't say who the item is for, or what type the item is (Progression/Useful/Filler/Trap), all of which are planned for later updates. - Fixed Archipelago Communism being named Archipelago Utopia, causing the location not to send. - Did lots of refactoring and code cleanup that's not interesting to users
### Installation Instructions: 1. Unzip Civ4-Archipelago-Mod into your Beyond the Sword mod folder (I've been testing it in the My Games one, but theoretically it should also work in the installation folder one; let me know if one or both work or don't work!), make sure the structure is Beyond the Sword/Mods/Civ4-Archipelago-Mod and that there isn't an extra folder in that structure. 2. Install the APWorld as normal.
### Play Instructions: 1. Run the Civilization IV client from Archipelago, but **do not connect from the client**; you'll do so in-game (and eventually I want to remove the ability to connect from the client) 2. Start a new Civ4 Beyond the Sword game as normal--**I highly recommend playing in windowed mode**, since this is an alpha and if the game freezes it can be difficult/impossible to close out of it if it's in full screen mode. 3. When you load in you'll get a popup saying to connect to the Archipelago Server: you do this by opening up the BUG options (the little dragon in the upper-right corner), entering in your information, then clicking "Save and Connect." If the connection is successful you'll get a popup that says "Successfully Connected," and you can play as normal. If you get an error, try connecting again, it most often means you don't have the client open or you're already connected in the client. Occasionally however the connection will be slow and you connect in the client but get an error in-game; in that case disconnect in the client and try again. **If this happens a lot to you let me know!**
### Gameplay Issues: 1. The settings aren't balanced at all, and it may make you do things like get 9 Great Scientists when all you have is the library or research Satellites before you have any economic techs. The Techsanity Era Gates setting should help the latter, and I'd highly recommend against large GPsanity numbers unless you have a lot of time to kill (though the added Great People in the pool will help). 2. There are a lot of debugging messages left in the mod. I removed some of them, but don't expect a clean feed. 3. When you're trying to select an "obsolete" wonder to build in the city screen, the building options will jump to the top of the building list due to the hacky way I've implemented that ability. I want to fix it eventually, but for now the easiest way to mitigate it is to use the wonder filter on the right side of the city list (the star), which will have it jump back to the start of the wonders, which hopefully won't make it jump. You can also use the "choose what to build next" dialog, or just select it without moving your mouse (use the scroll wheel). 4. The "AP" Unique Units can't be upgraded into, though they can be upgraded themselves. This is planned to be fixed in an upcoming update. 5. AP Unique Buildings are programmed assuming you don't have a "natural" Unique Building for your Civilization for purposes like avoiding duplicates of the same class of building, so if you use a Civilization other than AP World things could break. 6. If a building has a requirement to be built (such as the University), and you build an AP Unique Building version of it (such as the Seowon), you aren't able to build the original version anymore. There's no reason why you'd need to do this (the only vanilla building that's not strictly worse than the UB alternatives is the Theatre/Hippodrome, and that doesn't suffer the bug), but it's weird behavior.
### Technical Issues: 1. I had generation errors when creating solo/near-solo multiworlds with high Techsanity Era Gates values--I never tested with higher values with locations other than Techsanity enabled but keep that in mind if you're having trouble generating. 2. Whenever you close and reopen the game/a save file, you need to disconnect the client, and you should close and reopen the client to avoid missing checks. I plan to try and automate this in future updates. 3. There have been bug reports of items received/obtained while offline not properly appearing in-game and/or being sent to the multiworld when reconnecting. I think this is related to mismatching either mod or APworld versions, but I haven't fully found the root cause yet. 4. If you add Unique Buildings to the itempool, it causes a noticeable amount of lag when entering the city screen in some cases (due to the coding I need to make them work how I want them to). I think it scales with the amount of cities you have, but it also might be just a memory leak. If you experience this lag (or don't and think you would), let me know!
If you have any questions, bug reports, or things I forgot to mention, let me know in [the Civilization IV thread in the Archipelago Discord server](https://discord.com/channels/731205301247803413/1326231506682904576).
Github for the APWorld: https://github.com/VincentBorchardt/Archipelago/blob/main/worlds/civ_4/
